title: Stock Car Robot Lab

stages.title: Build the lower frame
stages.description: A flat open frame establishes the 10 × 10-inch concept envelope. Dimensions and material are placeholders, not fabrication instructions.
stages.question: What material and fastening method should survive wheel impacts without adding unnecessary weight?

stages.title: Add the differential drive
stages.description: Two powered wheels on a centered 8-inch track provide forward, reverse and in-place rotation. Small caster contacts are illustrative; real traction and scrub require testing.
stages.question: Should the concept use two drive wheels plus casters, or four driven wheels?

stages.title: Install power and emergency stop
stages.description: Battery, power distribution and a visible emergency-stop control occupy the rear deck. Battery chemistry, voltage, wiring and mounting are not selected.
stages.question: What battery and fuse architecture would meet the rules and the measured drivetrain load?

stages.title: Add control electronics
stages.description: A controller and motor driver sit on the open middle deck for access. Board models, connectors and computing power remain conceptual.
stages.question: Which controller can handle odometry, range sensing and camera/tag processing with margin?

stages.title: Add navigation sensors
stages.description: A raised camera, front/side range sensors and a low line array represent complementary sensing. Their fields of view and actual placements need calibration and rules review.
stages.question: Which sensors are necessary for reliable tag, line and obstacle observations under venue lighting?

stages.title: Add the tire-handling fork
stages.description: A short front fork illustrates a passive capture concept for the official-size tire. It is not a proven gripper and does not establish exchange or parking legality.
stages.question: Can a passive fork reliably acquire and retain the tire across its unknown initial poses and friction?

stages.title: Add the final-lap flag
stages.description: A lightweight mast and flag fit beneath the conceptual 12-inch starting-height ceiling. Deployment timing and school artwork are not modeled.
stages.question: Should the flag be fixed, hinged or actively deployed after the second lap?

stages.title: Protect wiring and inspect the envelope
stages.description: A cable cover completes the visual assembly. Real integration still needs strain relief, interference checks, fastener retention, mass measurement and emergency-stop testing.
stages.question: What physical inspection and low-speed tests should gate the first field run?

parts.name: Lower deck
parts.description: Conceptual structural deck; material and thickness are not selected.

parts.name: Carried spare tire
parts.description: Official tire proportions: approximately 68.18 mm OD and 40.30 mm bore. Red is the preload; the simulation substitutes blue after its conceptual dock event.

limitations: All robot part dimensions, placements and mechanisms are agent-authored visualization choices, not selected hardware or manufacturing CAD.

Physics is planar differential-drive motion with acceleration limits and discrete collision rejection, rendered in 3D. It omits suspension, tire slip, motor electrical dynamics, sensor noise, mechanism dynamics and 3D rigid-body contacts.
The stored south/north routes are conditional engineering examples to pit box 1 with an empty field, not complete three-lap missions or official legality determinations.
No obstacle vehicles, field tolerances, lap adjudication or scoring are simulated in this version.
Assembly playback is deterministic; field physics advances only while playing. Fast-forward changes simulated time rate, not solver fidelity.
